## Hack the planet

**The RF spectrum waterfall is gone.** In its place is a flight down a
corridor of mainframe towers, which is what happens when you type "hack the
planet" into the terminal on talkingsasquach.com and somebody decides it
should be on the detector too. The background is called **THE GIBSON** now,
in the same slot in Settings, so if you were already on RF SPECTRUM you have
already switched over.

The waterfall had one real problem: it showed you nothing when there was
nothing on the air, which is nearly always. A screen that is blank most of
the time is a screen you stop looking at, and a detector you stop looking at
is not doing its job. The Gibson moves whether or not anything is happening,
and does something unmistakable when something is.

**It is still a spectrum analyser.** The white trace across the middle is not
decoration: its x axis runs WiFi channels 1 to 13 and its height is that
channel's live activity, so real traffic genuinely deforms it. Down the right
edge there is now a **meter bridge** — thirteen labelled channel levels with
peak-hold marks — deliberately drawn *behind* the corridor, so the towers
sweep in front of it rather than it sitting permanently on top of the view.
And the light running down the lanes on the floor is real per-channel
traffic: a lane only carries packets when its channel does, so the floor
genuinely goes quiet when the band does.

**A detection locks onto a building.** When something new reaches the front
of the log, one tower floods with that detection's colour, takes a white
reticle, and the feed line at the bottom names it. It is chosen so that it
*arrives* — it appears in the distance and grows for the whole four seconds
it stays lit, rather than sweeping past you in the first second. Every window
in the city speeds up its blink at the same time.

**The city itself.** Thirteen thin towers on the horizon that never move,
with real window grids where some lights are on, some are off, and a quarter
of them switch on their own individual timers. Aircraft warning beacons on
the tall ones. A moon that gets half-eclipsed by whatever passes in front of
it. Searchlights sweeping the sky. Stars that twinkle but do not scroll,
because at that distance anything that scrolled would read as a fault.
Distant towers now fade into the sky's own colour rather than toward black —
on a 256-colour panel, black is where dim colours already land, so fading
that way reads as a building switching off rather than as one far away.

This is a heavier background than the waterfall it replaced. Measured on the
2.8" board it runs at **22fps** on the standard build; the experimental 80MHz
display option in the flasher is the one to use if you want it smoother.

**Ignoring a device now tells you it worked.** Tapping IGNORE on the log's
long-press menu closed the menu and otherwise looked exactly like tapping
CANCEL, with no evidence anything had happened. There is a small confirmation
panel now. It says **UN-IGNORED** when you tap it a second time, because that
button has always been a toggle and a popup that said IGNORED either way
would be worse than no popup at all.

**And the ignored list shows what you muted**, not just a column of MAC
addresses — the detection type on top in its own colour, the MAC underneath,
the same shape a LOG row has. Anything you ignored before this release will
show as UNKNOWN: the type was not recorded at the time, and the log entry
that would have answered the question scrolled out of the ring long ago.

**The web flasher works in Firefox.** It always would have — the page has
never sniffed your browser, it just asks whether Web Serial exists — but the
text was still telling Firefox users to go and find Chrome. It isn't now.

### The actually-useful part
- **Added**: THE GIBSON background, replacing the RF spectrum waterfall in the same Settings slot
- **Added**: channel meter bridge, thirteen live levels with peak hold, behind the corridor
- **Added**: floor traffic driven by real per-channel WiFi activity
- **Added**: detections lock onto a building, with a reticle and a named feed line
- **Added**: confirmation popup when you ignore or un-ignore a device
- **Changed**: the ignored-devices list shows detection type as well as MAC
- **Changed**: the flasher, README and FAQ list Firefox as supported
- **Note**: devices ignored before this release show as UNKNOWN — the type was never stored
